description:
Least-privilege capability set for the Conduit desktop webview. Every entry below has exactly one demonstrable caller under apps/desktop/src; the tests `capability_file_grants_nothing_the_frontend_cannot_use` and `every_tauri_plugin_the_frontend_imports_has_a_capability` (src-tauri/src/commands/file.rs) fail if that stops being true in either direction.

--

core:default
  Required by the whole app: `invoke()` in src/lib/tauri.ts, and `listen()` in
  src/hooks/useDiscovery.ts.

core:window:default
  Read-only window state plus the internal maximize toggle. Used via
  `getCurrentWindow()` in src/hooks/useAppShell.ts.

core:window:allow-show
  The ONLY mutating window permission kept. `useAppShell.ts` calls
  `win.show()` to reveal the window after the splash screen. The other seven
  window permissions (minimize, maximize, unmaximize, close, is-maximized,
  set-focus) were only used by src/components/layout/TitleBar.tsx, which is
  never imported — tauri.conf.json uses native `decorations: true`.

clipboard-manager:allow-read-text
  src/hooks/useClipboard.ts → `readText()`. The clipboard is a core feature;
  it is also where remote clipboard-sync payloads land, so this is the one
  permission that genuinely has to cross the boundary.

clipboard-manager:allow-write-text
  src/hooks/useClipboard.ts → `writeText()`.

dialog:allow-open
  The native file picker, in three places: src/App.tsx (pick + drag-drop),
  src/components/settings/FilesSection.tsx, and
  src/components/settings/AdvancedSection.tsx (Settings → Import). Tauri v2
  offers no way to scope a dialog permission to "the path the user just
  picked", so this is as narrow as the plugin allows.

fs:allow-read-text-file
  src/components/settings/AdvancedSection.tsx (Settings → Import) →
  `readTextFile()`. Unscoped for the same reason as the dialog: the file the
  user picks can be anywhere. Narrowed as far as the plugin allows — text
  files only, read-only, no write/mkdir/remove/watch. Previously this import
  had no Rust plugin and no permission at all, so the button never worked.

--

REMOVED, and why:

shell:allow-open
  `server/handlers/files.rs` broadcasts `FileComplete{ path }` with a
  sender-chosen path, the UI stores it as `saved_path`, and src/hooks/useFiles.ts
  handed it straight to `open()`. Any paired device could therefore choose the
  URI this machine opens, including `\\attacker\share\file` (an outbound SMB
  connection that discloses the NTLM hash) or a `file://` URI, with
  success/failure as a readable side channel. Opening now goes through the
  `open_downloaded_file` command, which looks the path up by transfer id from
  local state and refuses anything outside the download root.

process:default / process:allow-exit / process:allow-restart
  No exit or restart affordance exists: the frontend never imports
  `@tauri-apps/plugin-process`. The plugin stays registered in main.rs (the
  crate is in Cargo.toml) so a future restart control needs no plumbing, but
  the webview gets no reach into it.
